title: A Corporate Catering Service Agreement Beside the Client's Other Dining Services
content:
What a client holds elsewhere in the dining programme changes what a catering order costs and where it may be sent.

## Catering out of the client's own cafe kitchen

> Where the same client holds an active workplace cafe management contract whose service model permits catering out of the cafe kitchen, and the delivery site on the order is that cafe's site, the delivery fee is not charged because the food does not leave the building.

This clause is **no longer in force**.

> Where that cafe contract does not permit catering out of its kitchen, the order is produced at the district kitchen and the ordinary delivery fee applies however close the cafe is.

This clause is likewise **no longer in force**. The waiver of the **delivery fee** that these two retired clauses turned on stays recorded against every service level of the Corporate Catering Service Agreement except the Executive Hospitality Catering Account.

Whether the cafe kitchen at a site may be used for catering is a fact recorded against that site's cafe contract; where the cafe contract at the delivery site stands suspended, catering out of that kitchen stops with it and orders are produced at the district kitchen at the ordinary delivery fee until service resumes.

## Large parties and the banquet book

Where the same client holds an active private event and banquet agreement at the delivery site, an order whose guest count exceeds the largest guest count printed against the catering service level is placed as an event booking on that agreement instead, and the two are never run as one order. The guest count at which an order passes to the banquet book is the largest guest count printed against the catering service level, on every service level of the agreement.

## Micro markets

A catering agreement and an unattended micro market at the same site sit side by side without interaction, since a market sells to employees rather than to the client.
